meta.subtitle: Connecting marketing data, analytics and custom software
meta.speaker: Blagovest Iordanov

slides.title:
Smarter,
Scalable
Marketing

slides.body: How to connect marketing data, analytics and custom software into automation that grows with the business, shown through two real projects.

slides.title: About me
slides.name: Blagovest Iordanov
slides.role: Co-founder of ID Consult. I focus on data strategy, analytics infrastructure and technical implementation.

bullets.title: What I do
points: Digital marketing agency with clients in Bulgaria, the EU and the US
eCommerce, financial services, B2B and B2C
Tracking, server-side tagging, GA4, reporting pipelines
This past year: AI agents that write and maintain the code for me

paragraphs: Most marketing automation starts well and breaks once there are more clients, more accounts and more questions.

cards.label: Spreadsheets
cards.title: A report in Google Sheets
cards.body: 356,000 rows of Ads data in one sheet, with formulas nobody dares to touch.

cards.label: Scenarios
cards.title: Zap after Zap
cards.body: A separate scenario for every client. No change history, no tests, and nobody writes down what was decided.

cards.label: Prompts
cards.title: One-off chats
cards.body: The AI answers well once. Next month the context is explained from scratch.

blocks.label: Today's question
blocks.title: How can AI build systems, not just answers?
blocks.body: So that each new client costs less than the last one.

slides.title: Agenda
slides.body: Two real projects, one infrastructure decision and one framework for reuse.

items.title: Why I work in code repositories
items.body: The repo is the project's memory, for me and for the AI agent.

items.title: Project 1: Google Ads exporter
items.body: One shared model for 90+ ad accounts on BigQuery and dbt, plus a cost cut from $449 to $15 a month.

items.title: Cloud or workflow platform
items.body: When I pick Cloud Run and BigQuery, and when Make or n8n.

items.title: Project 2: healthcare client reporting
items.body: Shopify, WooCommerce, Google Ads and GA4 in a protected dashboard in 2 days. Where exports, APIs and MCP fit.

items.title: A framework for reuse
items.body: How to organise knowledge, tools and business cases.

blocks.text: Why I work in code repositories

paragraphs: I don't write the code by hand. I write the tasks, decisions and rules. An AI agent (Codex, Claude Code) implements them in the repo, and Git keeps everything.

cards.title: History
cards.body: Every change is a commit with a reason. The exporter has 74, and each one says why, not just what.

cards.title: Memory
cards.body: AGENTS.md, contracts and decisions in docs/. The agent reads them before every task and doesn't repeat old mistakes.

cards.title: Tests
cards.body: 155 dbt tests in the exporter, 38 unit tests in the client project. Bad data never reaches the client.

cards.title: Reuse
cards.body: A new project reads older repos as references but never changes them.

blocks.text: Read docs/CONTRACTS.md as durable project memory.

slides.title: Project 1: Google Ads exporter
paragraphs: gads-export-all: one shared reporting model for all of the agency's clients.

slides.title: Google Ads exporter
slides.body: Goal: one reporting layer, not a separate sheet for every client.

items.label: Team
items.title: The agency
items.body: PPC managers who watch dozens of accounts every day.

items.label: Input
items.title: Google Ads Data Transfer
items.body: Raw export into BigQuery, 94 accounts in config, in several currencies (EUR, BGN, USD, GBP, RON, MXN).

items.label: Output
items.title: Reports and alerts
items.body: Management hub, keyword and search term audits, budget pacing, alerts and a daily Telegram summary.

items.label: Rule
items.title: Raw data stays untouched
items.body: Settings live in config tables, logic in SQL marts, and the app only filters and displays.

slides.success: Differences between clients live in configuration, not in copies of the code.

items.label: raw
items.title: gads_raw
items.body: Google Ads DTS export. Read-only.

items.label: cfg
items.title: Configuration
items.body: Accounts, thresholds, groups, ECB exchange rates.

items.label: stg
items.title: Standardisation
items.body: 17 staging models that normalise the sources.

items.label: mart
items.title: Reporting logic
items.body: 17 marts, each with client_id, account_id and report_date.

items.label: app
items.title: Delivery
items.body: FastAPI reports with Google login, plus a Telegram bot.

blocks.label: Orchestration
blocks.title: One Cloud Run job, triggered by Cloud Scheduler
blocks.body: Freshness check → alert on dropped accounts → ECB rates → dbt build → dbt test → Telegram summary. Stops at the first failure.

slides.title: Cloud or workflow platform
slides.body: It isn't either-or. The question is how much data there is, how often the rules change, and who will maintain it.

columns.label: Make / n8n / Zapier
columns.title: Workflow platform
items: Little data, event → action (lead → CRM → Slack)
Business users can change the steps themselves
Limits on operations and run time
Hard to test, hard to diff versions

columns.label: Cloud Run + BigQuery + dbt
columns.title: Cloud infrastructure
items: Hundreds of thousands of rows a day, years of history
Rules that must be verified (currencies, attribution, ROAS)
Tests, staging, rollback to a previous image
Cost measured in GB, not in task counts
The AI agent writes the code, so "hard to maintain" is no longer an argument

slides.title: Demo: BigQuery costs from $449 to $15
slides.body: How the AI agent finds where the money goes, measures it, and proves nothing is lost.

slides.title: Result
slides.body: Measured in billed bytes from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS, not estimated.

metrics.label: account/date pairs lost in the A/B check
hidden gap in ECB rates, found by a new test

points: The optimisation surfaced an old bug. A new coverage test showed the ECB feed had stopped for 13 days, leaving USD/GBP accounts with an empty cost_eur.
Rejected ideas are also written down in the repo, with the reason.

slides.title: Project 2: Client from the healthcare industry
paragraphs: Building on top: client reporting on the exporter, in two days.

slides.title: Healthcare client reporting
slides.body: The ask: replace a manual spreadsheet with a daily dashboard by country, campaign and year over year.

items.label: Client
items.title: EU eCommerce, healthcare
items.body: Migrated from WooCommerce to Shopify, with two Google Ads accounts (an old BGN one and a new EUR one).

items.label: Input
items.title: 5 sources
items.body: Shopify API, Woo order history in Sheets, Google Ads export, GA4 BigQuery export and ECB rates.

items.label: Output
items.title: Protected dashboard
items.body: Business ROAS by country, Ads by country → campaign → month, campaigns with YoY. Google login access.

items.label: Foundation
items.title: Reused parts
items.body: Ads marts from the exporter, Shopify extractor patterns, the UI hub from another client.

slides.success: The second project was cheap because the first one left behind tools and documented decisions.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.title: The first commit is a document, not code
blocks.body: The discovery report lists what was checked, what wasn't, and which decisions belong to a human.

slides.title: Demo: when the numbers don't match
slides.body: Discovery, decisions, then a finding: the shared export has no countries for Performance Max.

slides.title: Exports, APIs and AI connectors
slides.body: Each source comes in through the most stable channel available. Everything meets in BigQuery.

center.label: Warehouse
center.title: BigQuery
center.body: raw → core → mart, with provenance on every row

nodes.label: Data export
nodes.title: Google Ads DTS
nodes.body: Daily export of all accounts. Cheap and stable.

nodes.label: API
nodes.title: Shopify GraphQL
nodes.body: Orders, refunds, country. The token is renewed every day.

nodes.label: MCP
nodes.title: Google Ads MCP
nodes.body: Fills the gap the export can't cover (PMax by country).

nodes.label: File
nodes.title: Legacy CSV / Sheets
nodes.body: One-off import with SHA-256 and row numbers.

nodes.label: API
nodes.title: ECB rates
nodes.body: Daily rates, carried forward up to 30 days during outages.

blocks.text: Exports are the foundation, MCP is the instrument

cards.label: Data export
cards.title: For volume and history
cards.body: Every day, every account, no human in the loop. The base of every report.

cards.label: AI connector (MCP)
cards.title: For exploration and gaps
cards.body: The agent queries the live API, compares and proves. That's how we found 291 days of cost mismatch.

cards.label: MCP in production
cards.title: Only under contract
cards.body: Fixed account, row cap, reconciliation to the cent, and temporary status until the export is fixed.

blocks.label: Rule
blocks.title: A connector doesn't replace the warehouse
blocks.body: MCP responses are saved as artifacts with provenance and loaded through the same checks as any other source.

slides.title: Artifacts in the repo
slides.body: What stays after the chat. Shortened, anonymised excerpts from the real files.

artifacts.title: AGENTS.md
artifacts.body: The rules the agent follows on every task.

artifacts.title: Discovery report
artifacts.body: Gaps, risks and questions for a human.

artifacts.title: Ads cost reconciliation
artifacts.body: Why DTS and the API report different cost for the same campaign.

artifacts.title: Cost optimisation
artifacts.body: 4 changes, measured in GB and dollars.

slides.title: The trust boundary
slides.body: AI prepares, executes and verifies. A human decides what the data means for the business.
slides.boundary: AI builds and proves; the human sets the rules

ai.label: The AI agent does
items: Discovery of sources, schemas and gaps
Reconciliation to the cent and A/B checks
Documents every decision in the repo

human.label: The human decides
items: The migration date and which source takes precedence
Who gets access to the client's data
Whether to trade a safety stage for a 50% lower bill

cards.title: Missing is not zero
cards.body: An empty day in the data is a gap to investigate, not zero spend.

cards.title: IDs, not names
cards.body: Campaigns get renamed. The key is account + campaign ID; the name is just a label.

cards.title: Contracts are memory
cards.body: A decision that isn't written down will be "fixed" by the next agent.

cards.title: Measure in bytes
cards.body: One view, joined by 10 marts, was 70% of the bill.

cards.title: Check before publishing
cards.body: If a run fails, the client sees the last good data, not broken data.

cards.title: References are read-only
cards.body: A new project copies patterns and never touches working systems.

slides.title: Framework
paragraphs: How projects become reusable solutions without losing each business's specifics.

cards.label: Knowledge
cards.title: What we know
cards.body: AGENTS.md, CONTRACTS.md, discovery, recorded decisions and rejected ideas. The agent reads them on every task.

cards.label: Tools
cards.title: What we work with
cards.body: Exporters, dbt models, the FX pipeline, MCP clients, deploy scripts. One repo, many clients.

cards.label: Business cases
cards.title: What we solve
cards.body: A separate repo for each client case. References are read, not blindly copied.

cards.label: Specifics
cards.title: What's different
cards.body: Config tables, revenue definition, migration boundary, access list. Decided with the client.

blocks.label: The effect
blocks.title: Each new client costs less than the last
blocks.body: The exporter took months to build. The healthcare client project, built on top of it, took two days.

slides.title: Playbook
slides.body: The same order for every new client.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.body: The agent checks the sources and records what is proven and what isn't.

steps.title: Decisions
steps.body: A human answers the open questions, and the answers become a contract in the repo.

steps.title: Build on the shared layer
steps.body: Specifics go into config; the shared layer stays untouched.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.body: Tests, reconciliation and A/B checks against the old source.

steps.title: Schedule it
steps.body: A Cloud Run job and Scheduler, publishing only if the checks pass.

steps.title: Extract
steps.body: Anything that repeats goes back into the tools and the knowledge.

paragraphs: Pick one report you build by hand every month.
Create a repo with an AGENTS.md, and let the agent investigate first and build second.

blocks.label: This week
blocks.title: One source, one test, one scheduled job.
blocks.body: Then the next client already has something to build on.
